subject: PO tokenization & weekly invoice rail for enterprise pricing
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@orionlogistics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@orionlogistics.com>, Orion Logistics AP <ap@orionlogistics.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO tokenization & weekly invoice rail for enterprise pricing

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — product looked great and the team is excited. Procurement has a few requirements we need to validate before we can finalize the 12-month commitment:

- We typically require a single blanket PO that contains a purchasable token we can reference on weekly invoices (our ERP needs a deterministic token per service). Can Redwood accept a PO that uses a custom field (e.g., PURCHASE_ORDER_TOKEN) and emit that token on each invoice line?
- Our AP prefers weekly invoice statements to match our payment runs; we understand Redwood invoices monthly by default — any flexibility here?
- Net terms: our default is Net60, but we can consider Net45 if discount triggers are tighter.
- We attach our standard PO sample and an ERP mapping file. Please confirm the fields you need so we can circulate internally.

Finally, finance asked whether committed-discount buckets must be applied at invoice level or at deal level (we have multi-entity billing). Looking for the simplest approach that preserves our audit trail.

Attaching: Orion_PO_sample.pdf, Orion_ERP_mapping.xlsx

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Orion Logistics
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@orionlogistics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@orionlogistics.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO tokenization & weekly invoice rail for enterprise pricing

Hi Marta — great to meet you and thanks for the files. Looping Vivek (finance) and Kimberly (customer success) to iron out mapping and billing ops.

Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can accept a blanket PO that carries a PURCHASE_ORDER_TOKEN field. We will emit that token as an invoice header and as an optional line-level field (invoice metadata) so your ERP can reconcile by token.
- Weekly statement support: we can enable weekly statements as a customer configuration, but it does impose a different reconciliation cadence and minimum invoice size for efficiency. Our proposal: pilot weekly statements for the first 90 days, limited to invoices < $50k per week; otherwise we consolidate to a weekly statement with line-level detail.
- Net terms: we can do Net60; however the committed discount structure shifts slightly. For a 12-month committed spend >= $600k we offer an 8% committed discount at deal level; if you'd like Net45 in lieu of Net60 we can increase to 10% committed discount.

What we need from your side to proceed:
1) Confirm the exact PO field names your ERP will populate (purchase_order_token, billing_entity_id, cost_center, GL_code).
2) A sample blanket PO with the token populated (you sent that — thanks).
3) Which Orion entity will be billed for the committed bucket (single entity vs. multi-entity mapping).

I've attached our PO field spec (redwood_po_field_spec.csv) showing required/optional fields and an example payload for our billing system. If that looks good, I can draft a short amendment to the SOW to capture weekly statement pilot and discount tier.

Next steps: Vivek and I will propose exact wording for the amendment and the discount trigger. Kimberly — can your team own the pilot logistics for the first 90 days?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_po_field_spec.csv

To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@orionlogistics.com>, Orion Logistics AP <ap@orionlogistics.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO tokenization & weekly invoice rail for enterprise pricing

Ben — thanks for the quick reply. A couple of clarifications from AP and legal: 

- Our ERP will populate PURCHASE_ORDER_TOKEN, BILLING_ENTITY_ID, and COST_CENTER. GL_code will come from a separate mapping file (we attached Orion_ERP_mapping.xlsx). Can you consume GL_code as an optional line attribute?
- Regarding weekly statements: we need the statement to show week start/end dates and a single statement balance per billing entity for each run. Line-level detail is required for audits (SKU-level).
- On discounts: finance would prefer the 10% if we can get Net45 — is that firm for the 12-month commitment? If so we can fast-track approval.
- Also asking if Redwood supports an early-pay incentive (we offer 1.5% to vendors) for invoices paid within 30 days — is Redwood open to an early-pay credit in addition to committed discount?

Attached: Orion_ERP_mapping.xlsx (sample GL mapping), Orion_PO_sample.pdf (with token example).

If you can confirm by end of day we will present to the CFO tomorrow.

Best,
Marta
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@orionlogistics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO tokenization & weekly invoice rail for enterprise pricing

Marta — appreciate the fast turnaround. Vivek and I reviewed this with Finance and here is a practical proposal we can put in the amendment: 

- PO field support: we will consume PURCHASE_ORDER_TOKEN, BILLING_ENTITY_ID, COST_CENTER, and an optional GL_CODE field. If GL mapping is in a separate file we will accept GL_CODE on the invoice; otherwise we will include line-level SKU metadata that your ERP team can map.
- Weekly statements: Redwood will enable a weekly statement rail showing week start/end, statement balance per billing entity, plus full line-level SKU detail exported as CSV for reconciliation. This will be enabled as a 90-day pilot; after the pilot we will either continue weekly statements or default back to monthly based on operational load.
- Pricing/discounts: we can confirm the 10% committed discount for a signed 12-month commitment >= $600k if Redwood receives Net45 terms. If you choose Net60, the committed discount will be 8%.
- Early-pay: we can offer an early-pay credit of 1.0% (applies to invoices paid within 30 days) in addition to the committed discount. We cannot combine the early-pay credit to exceed a cap of 12% effective discount on any invoice.

Attachments & approvals: I've attached the PO field spec again and a simple amendment draft I can push to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/tx/AMEND-ORION-2027 (draft).

Next steps (recommended):
1) Confirm whether Orion accepts Net45 + 10% committed discount.
2) Confirm billing entity that will be the primary invoiced entity for the committed bucket.
3) AP to confirm sample weekly statement format (we will send a template).
4) If the above are OK, I'll issue the DocuSign amendment and Kimberly will coordinate the pilot onboarding (billing and AP test run).

Kimberly — can you schedule a 30-minute pilot walkthrough with Marcus and the AP team tomorrow?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
